text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Debt and bond future prices continued their consolidation in early trade as dealers said the slightly lower course of U.S. bonds in European trade had exerted a negative influence. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.14, up 0.22 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts drifted higher in lacklustre trade -- the calm before the budget storm next Tuesday, dealers said. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-28/32, up 6/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures bore the brunt of the franc slide early on but soon regained their composure and moved back in step with the Bund market to end the week a fraction higher than they were last Friday. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.74, up 0.10 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets ended firm as the market held its breath in the expectation the lira would return to Europe's exchange rate mechanism at the weekend. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.97, up 0.70 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries continued to trade in very narrow ranges midday, amid dull and lackluster dealings, as the market counts down the hours to the weekend. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 115-13/32, down 4/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.43 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese Government Bond futures contract ended a volatile session with handsome gains as late short-covering outweighed speculative selling. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 124.63, up 0.11 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Following the excitement in the emerging market sector over Russia's debut Eurobond launch on Thursday, activity today simmered down. Russia's Eurobond spread over U.S. Treasuries held steady in the secondary market. Caisse Nationale du Credit Agricole launched a 100 million Ecu January 2003 zero-coupon bond. Abbey National set a 1.0 billion French franc Tec-10 linked 10-year bond.
